title: ftblocks: fine-tune the last N DINOv2-base blocks + readout per fold (nested selection)
status: frozen BEFORE any grid run; only smoke tests (fold-0 N=0 reproduction, 20-step N=4/N=2 runs scored on the fold-0 INNER-VAL set, never on a test fold) and the timing bench have been run
question: Does fine-tuning the last N transformer blocks of frozen-DINOv2-base (+ final LayerNorm + our ASPP readout) on each fold's 800 maps close the gap from ours_scratch_s0 (CC 0.8975) towards msdb_adapt / sum_ft (~0.92) at unchanged inference cost (same graph, 221 GFLOPs)?

base_readout_inputs.checkpoint: facebook/dinov2-base (HF transformers AutoModel, sdpa attention, no register tokens)
base_readout_inputs.input: PIL RGB, bilinear resize 448x448, /255, ImageNet mean (0.485,0.456,0.406) / std (0.229,0.224,0.225), interpolate_pos_encoding=True
base_readout_inputs.tokens: last_hidden_state = final LayerNorm(output of block 12); CLS dropped; 1024 patch tokens -> 768x32x32
base_readout_inputs.readout: ours_lib.ReadoutHead('full'): ASPP 768->128 (dilations 1,3,6,12 + GAP) + 1x1 head + learned 16x16 centre bias; 3,721,089 params

block_cache.why_two_depths: N=4 starts from block 8, N=2 from block 10; caching both avoids a frozen forward of blocks 9-10 in every N=2 step (6.3 GB total)

verification.summary: CPU replay of the remaining frozen blocks + final norm on the cached block outputs reproduces last_hidden_state bit-for-bit (max abs diff 0.0) and the fp16 cast equals the existing readout cache in every element for all 1000 images at both depths; on MPS the replay deviates from the CPU by <= 2.1e-4 absolute (features up to |19.6|, i.e. ~1e-5 relative)

protocol.outer_split: splits/kfold_seed0.json, 5 folds x 200 test ids; train = the other 4 folds in run_row.py order
protocol.seeds: fold k: torch.manual_seed(k) immediately before the readout is built (all configs: same readout init); data-order rng numpy default_rng(k), including the base recipe's start-of-training 200-image draw
protocol.N0: the unchanged base recipe: ours_lib.train on the fp16 feature cache (AdamW lr 3e-4 wd 1e-4 constant, 60 epochs, batch 16, KL + (1 - CC) at 64x64)
protocol.N_gt_0: cached frozen block-(12-N) output -> trainable blocks 12-N+1..12 -> trainable final LayerNorm -> readout. One AdamW: readout lr 3e-4 wd 1e-4 constant; backbone blocks + final norm lr_bb, wd 0.05 (all their parameters), linear warmup lr_bb*(s+1)/W for s < W = round(0.05 * total steps), then constant (the readout's schedule). Same loss, batch 16, data order, 60 epochs (inner 2400 steps, outer 3000 steps)
protocol.precision: fp32 everywhere (no autocast; bf16 was timed for information only and is NOT used)
protocol.augmentation: none (horizontal flip is NOT in the pre-registered grid and is therefore not used)
protocol.finalizer: Gaussian sigma from {0,2,4,6,8,10,12} by mean CC on a random 200-image subset of the run's training ids (inner: of inner-train; final: of the 800 outer training ids), drawn from the data-order rng after training
protocol.per_run_checkpoint: cache/ftblocks/runs/<run>.json written atomically after each run; existing runs are skipped (a crash loses at most the run in progress); nested final models saved to cache/ftblocks/models/

inner_split.rule: perm = numpy default_rng(100 + k).permutation(800) over the outer training ids in run_row order; inner_train = tr[perm[:640]], inner_val = tr[perm[640:]]

selection.metric: mean inner-val CC (160 images) after the inner-train sigma
selection.rule: best = max mean inner-val CC; every config with CC >= best - 0.001 is tied; select the first tied config in simplicity order = grid order (smaller N first, then lower lr_bb)
selection.final: retrain the selected config on all 800 outer training ids (3000 steps), sigma on 200 of them, score the 200 outer test ids ONCE

rows.ours_ftblocks_nested: PRIMARY. Per-fold selected config (recorded per fold).
rows.ours_ftblocks_global: SECONDARY, transparency only: one config chosen by the same rule on the inner-val CC averaged over the 5 folds; run on all 5 outer folds; final runs are shared with the nested row where the config coincides (identical code, seeds and data).

optional_distill.trigger: run ONLY if in >= 4 of 5 folds the nested selection beats the N0 control on inner validation, i.e. the selected config is not N0 (by the tie rule this implies its inner-val CC exceeds N0's by more than 0.001)
optional_distill.recipe: fold-k nested config + the distill_pitt recipe of scripts/distill/train_students.py: each step the base 16 ADD1000 training ids with GT + 16 Pitt pool images (2,499) with teacher-k targets (cache/distill/targets/pitt_t64.npy, MSDB head adapted on fold k's 800 training maps), one forward of 32, loss = L(GT) + 1.0 L(Pitt); Pitt stream Cycler(default_rng(100000 + k)); 3000 steps; sigma by the base rule on ADD1000 training images
optional_distill.pitt_cache: frozen block outputs of the 2,499 Pitt pool images computed exactly like the ADD1000 cache (cache_blocks.py --set pitt) in fp16 (3.9 GB per depth) at depth 12-N of the selected N; if folds select both N=2 and N=4 only depth 8 is cached and N=2 folds apply frozen blocks 9-10 on the fly for BOTH streams (ADD1000 then also starts from block 8; mathematically identical model)
optional_distill.no_selection: no further tuning; the row is scored once per test fold

statistics.code: scripts/ftblocks/stats_ftblocks.py; holm, nb_test, rank_biserial, compare, vec, fold_means, describe, seed_avg executed verbatim from scripts/compile/compile_results.py (ast extraction)
statistics.tests: paired bootstrap 95% CI (5000) of the mean per-image difference, per-image Wilcoxon signed-rank, fold-level Nadeau-Bengio corrected t (df 4), fold SD ddof 1; differences = ftblocks row minus reference
statistics.secondary_family: each existing secondary row (global, distill) vs the same 7 references; Holm within the family
statistics.holm: within each family, separately per metric (CC, SIM, KLD) and test (Wilcoxon, NB)
statistics.headline: ours_ftblocks_nested - ours_scratch_s0 on CC (primary comparison)

optional_distill_h_approx.note: not measured: assumes a 32-image step costs 2x the measured 16-image step

timing.note: estimates exclude time spent waiting for the shared MPS lock

fallback.rule: if the full-grid estimate exceeds 10.0 h, run the fallback grid (N0, N2_lr3e-05, N4_lr3e-05): lr_bb = 1e-5 is dropped; everything else (nesting, seeds, selection rule, final retrain, rows, statistics) is unchanged
fallback.why_not_select_on_fold0_only: selecting once on fold 0's inner split and applying the config to folds 1-4 would use images of folds 1-4's test sets (they are fold 0's training ids) for a choice made for those folds, violating the mandatory nesting; rejected
fallback.why_drop_lr1e-5: keeps both depths N=2 and N=4 (the question) and strict nesting; at 2400-3000 steps lr 1e-5 moves the blocks least, so it is the least likely to change the answer
